note: Billionaire Life prototype. Every date and number below appears in at least one cited source. Situations and outcomes are summarized in our own words and simplified. Alternatives are generic choices for the game, not claims about what he considered.

person.name: Jeff Bezos
person.role: Founder and Executive Chair of Amazon
person.bio: Founded Amazon in 1994 and has chaired its board ever since. He was CEO from May 1996 to July 2021, then became Executive Chair. He also founded Blue Origin, owns The Washington Post and chairs the Bezos Earth Fund.

bioSource.title: Amazon 2026 proxy statement (Form DEF 14A), director biography

decisions.title: The Wall Street job or the online store?
decisions.situation: You joined investment firm D. E. Shaw & Co. in December 1990 and became a senior vice president in 1992. You have an idea for a company that sells books over the internet.

options.label: Stay at the firm and keep climbing
Quit and start an online bookstore
Build it as a side project, keep the job

decisions.actual: He left D. E. Shaw in June 1994 and founded Amazon.com in July 1994. The site began selling books in July 1995.
decisions.outcome: Amazon went public in May 1997 at $18 a share, after 1996 sales of $15.7 million. For 2025 it reported total net sales of $716.9 billion.

decisions.title: Charge a yearly fee for fast shipping?
decisions.situation: Your store already wins customers with low prices and free shipping. Fast, express delivery is still an extra cost people pay order by order, and giving it away unlimited would be expensive for you in the short term.

options.label: Launch a flat yearly membership with free two-day shipping
Keep charging for express shipping on each order
Offer free express shipping only on big orders

decisions.actual: In February 2005 Amazon launched Amazon Prime, its first membership program: $79 a year for unlimited free two-day shipping with no minimum order. He admitted it would cost the company in the short term.
decisions.outcome: In his 2017 shareholder letter he wrote that no customer ever asked Amazon to create Prime. In his April 2021 letter he said Amazon had more than 200 million Prime members. In 2025 Amazon's subscription sales, which include Prime fees, were $49.6 billion.

sources.title: Amazon.com announces record free cash flow; introduces Amazon Prime

decisions.title: Rent out your computer systems?
decisions.situation: You are an online retailer. To run your own websites you have built large, reliable, low-cost data storage systems. Outside software developers could use the same thing.

options.label: Keep the systems in-house as an edge for the store
Sell the same infrastructure to any developer
License the software to big tech companies

decisions.actual: On March 14, 2006 Amazon Web Services launched Amazon S3, a storage service that gave any developer the same infrastructure Amazon used for its own sites.
decisions.outcome: In 2025 AWS sales rose 20% to $128.7 billion, with $45.6 billion in operating income.

decisions.title: Buy a famous newspaper?
decisions.situation: The Washington Post Company, led by chairman Donald Graham, has decided to sell the paper after years of newspaper-industry struggles. Its leaders wonder if another owner might be better for it.

options.label: Pass; newspapers are a shrinking business
Buy it personally, separate from Amazon

decisions.actual: In August 2013 he agreed to buy The Washington Post and related publishing businesses for $250 million, through a company of his own, not Amazon. He asked the paper's top leaders to stay on.
decisions.outcome: The sale closed on October 1, 2013 to his company Nash Holdings. The seller renamed itself Graham Holdings. Amazon's 2026 proxy still lists the Post among the businesses he owns.

decisions.title: How big a bet on climate?
decisions.situation: You run Amazon, which has just pledged to use 100% renewable energy by 2030 and reach carbon neutrality by 2040. Some Amazon employees have pushed for more. You are deciding how much of your own fortune to put toward climate.

options.label: Pledge $10 billion to a new climate fund
Leave it to Amazon's own climate programs

decisions.actual: On February 17, 2020 he announced the Bezos Earth Fund on Instagram, committing $10 billion of his own money to fund scientists, activists and groups working to protect the natural world.
decisions.outcome: On November 16, 2020 he named the first 16 grantees, sharing $791 million; five groups got $100 million each. Amazon's 2026 proxy says the $10 billion is to be given out as grants within this decade.
